gap_records.summary: Required candidate file for `native_godot_project` is unverified.

acceptance_requirements: Pass the unchanged frozen game_title_entry_review check through independent Host/Tester observation.
Deliver the title-entry behaviors in operator-ui-story.md module 1 and PRD 6.1, 6.4, 6.6, 6.9 and 6.10 while preserving existing gameplay and save continuity.
Verify ordinary pointer and keyboard operation, 1920×1080 and 1280×720 layouts, and Chinese text at 100%, 150% and 200% scale.
deferred_items: Full settings, pause and save-page redesign remains assigned to game_settings_pause; this increment provides a functional title settings destination for existing preferences.
Gameplay HUD, task journal, enemy/NPC template expansion, illustrated opening, old-lamp training and later chapters remain subsequent modules.
Backlog gaps gap:native_godot_project and gap:host_godot_boot remain mandatory and unverified, without separate tasks or targets in this iteration.
Historical Forest performance and other unresolved quality findings retain their existing acceptance; title work does not close them.
implied_completion: A load-slot preview reads metadata without loading that history into the active adventure or rewriting saves.
Entry is complete only after resource loading and safe world initialization finish; a completed resource progress bar alone does not establish player readiness.
Returning to title releases gameplay input and stops world simulation while preserving committed progress and failure state.
A structurally valid automatic save with zero lives resumes Game Over; it must not be mistaken for a fresh adventure or grant a free retry.
mandatory_objectives: Own gap:game_title_entry_review exactly once in one cohesive title-entry task.
Replace direct gameplay boot and the unavailable-title return path with a real title journey.
Preserve Forest, village actors, player animation and equipment bindings, Snaiel combat, sword/bow training, dialogue, rewards and saved histories.
task_specification.objective: Deliver a finished, state-bound title screen and ordinary boot-to-game, load, settings, return-to-title and exit journeys for 艾洛的冒险, using the existing playable world and authoritative save interfaces.

diagnosis.root_cause: The candidate's project.godot starts Preview.tscn directly. preview_controller.gd immediately instantiates Forest, creates gameplay actors and loads the automatic save. Its _show_failure_title() only displays an unavailable-title message. A standalone title and entry lifecycle is therefore absent in source, rather than merely awaiting cosmetic improvement. Existing save validation, restoration, adventure reset, pause ownership and serif theme provide reusable interfaces. Current runtime quality remains unverified; the historical title-stub observation supports diagnosis but does not constitute current acceptance.

stop_conditions: Stop this increment after the two task completion conditions and focused Developer checks are satisfied; leave formal phase closure to Host and Tester.
If menu-source compatibility, artwork rights, import dependencies or safe initialization cannot be established, preserve the candidate and report the precise unresolved dependency.
If registered replay, frame, state or audio observation cannot demonstrate a required outcome, retain that outcome as blocked or unverified; do not substitute candidate-authored pass flags.
Do not expand into deferred modules or waive frozen gameplay, failure-recovery, presentation or performance acceptance.

strategy.rationale: Build one title-entry module around the existing adventure rather than reconstructing gameplay. Inspection found reusable MainMenu submenu/focus behavior and SceneLoader resource-status handling in the local Maaack Godot-Menus-Template bundle, plus an existing candidate serif theme and Kenney frame bindings. Use that menu bundle as the primary reusable foundation, adapting its main-menu, focus, confirmation and loading responsibilities through a product entry/save adapter. Its industrial background, FPS typography, branding, hard-coded margins, default new-game behavior and loader failure handling do not meet this product's requirements and require adaptation. Preserve the already integrated Snaiel components and village controller; the selected combat and dialogue templates do not supply,

code: Developer verifies the adopted menu dependency closure, pinned Godot compatibility, resource references and release-default debug settings through registered import/parse checks.
Inspect the actual startup and return bindings, read-only slot-preview path, selected-slot propagation, failed-entry rollback and removal of the unavailable-title stub.
Check preservation of existing save formats and manual slots, plus existing player, Forest, dialogue, training and Snaiel integration interfaces.
runtime: Developer runs one bounded smoke: boot title, submenu/back, New Game or Continue, safe world readiness, return to title and re-entry; report actual checks and unresolved outcomes.

Host/Tester independently exercise no-save, valid-auto, two distinct manual histories, empty/unreadable slot, New Game cancel/confirm, settings/back, real exit/restart and zero-life failure continuation using ordinary pointer and keyboard input.

Observe title before and after gameplay: gameplay must be absent or stopped, mouse/focus ownership correct, repeated activation single-shot, and held confirmation inputs must not trigger attacks on entry.

After loading, compare actual quest, equipment, arrows, XP, rewards and lives with the selected history. Verify New Game begins unarmed with initial facts and preserves both manual histories; return/restart grants no rewards or lives. Valid depleted automatic history returns to Game Over; early manual loading restores its own history.
visual: Host/Tester capture title normal/focused/disabled states, load slots, confirmation, settings return, genuine loading/error feedback and returned title at 1920×1080 and 1280×720 with 100%, 150% and 200% Chinese text.

Compare ordinary rendered views with main-menu-v1.png for hierarchy, parchment/metal ornament, title prominence and disabled Continue, and main-menu-background-v1.png for crop, river-valley atmosphere and readable safe area. Reference screenshots remain comparison material; buttons and values must be live UI.

Inspect every newly bound visible family for source quality, license/provenance, real runtime visibility, clean transparency, scale and the frozen diversity rules. Treat the full-bleed title background as one semantic singleton; obtain its missing qualification rather than treating the asset-pool preview label as acceptance.

Hear or capture focus, confirm, back, unavailable and failure feedback at normal speed; verify mute/reduced-motion preferences, no disabled-action success sound and no overlapping world audio after returning to title.

done_when: Ordinary launch presents a finished Aelor title with five actions, coherent river-valley/old-lamp art, serif Chinese/Latin typography, restrained motion and sound, and distinguishable normal, hover, focus, pressed and disabled states; title, load and confirmation layouts remain readable and operable at both required resolutions and all three text scales, with no player-facing diagnostic content.

Ordinary input completes New Game, Continue, two-slot Load, functional Settings/back, return to title and software Exit with truthful loading/error feedback; manual histories survive New Game, selected histories restore their actual facts, zero-life continuation remains Game Over, title never simulates gameplay, and adjacent dialogue, equipment, combat, rewards and recovery retain their existing .

investigation.expected_observation: The menu foundation can run with complete dependencies while the product adapter exclusively owns adventure state; no Forest actors exist or advance on title, and one entry action produces one safely initialized world. Any class/configuration or loading failure is observable before broader adoption.
investigation.hypothesis: The reusable menu focus and loading mechanisms can be adapted independently of the source project's FPS skin and configuration authority.
investigation.probe: Run a bounded Developer compatibility smoke after integrating the menu dependency closure: boot title, open/back one submenu, activate one real entry, return to title, and inspect source-bound active route, initialization status and world processing.

research_assessment.reason: Actual local menu and loader code was inspected and compared with the candidate's direct boot, placeholder return and existing save/theme methods. Dependency closure, pinned-runtime compatibility and artwork qualification remain Developer checks. Compare the supplied background and existing frames with the local menu's
research_assessment.target_capability: Title navigation, scene loading, save previews and responsive themed presentation

resource_strategy.reason: Adopt and adapt the inspected local Maaack menu/focus/loading foundation and qualify the operator-supplied title background. Reuse existing live dialogue_theme.tres font bindings and Kenney frames. Preserve the current Forest, actor and Snaiel bindings without another map/controller transfer.

risk_note.summary: The most likely insufficient-evidence outcome is a visually complete title whose transition does not prove selected-save restoration, safe spawn, absent background simulation or correct zero-life recovery. The local loader also has configuration dependencies and incomplete product error recovery.
risk_note.validation: Pair independent ordinary-input sequences with active-route/loading/readiness observations, authoritative save facts and world-processing observations; capture intermediate loading, returned-title and failed-save states as well as the final world. Require heard or captured UI audio separately.
risk_note.why_now: This increment changes the boot and recovery boundary around an already integrated game; incorrect ownership can silently reset progress or resume gameplay behind the menu.
